label: Pie Rouge des Plaines

about.text: A French red-and-white dual-purpose breed begun in Brittany around 1970 by crossing Armorican cattle with German Rotbunt and Dutch Meuse-Rhine-Yssel stock, aiming at a dairy breed with good meat qualities. Brittany holds about 80% of the herd, with some in Normandy and the Massif Central. Its milk is about 4.3% fat and 3.3% protein.

sources.text: Wikipedia, drawing on Dervillé et al. 2009 and Porter et al. 2016. The 80% share and the regions are from Dervillé et al. 2009 as cited there.
Wikipedia: farmers in Brittany's three western départements began the breed around 1970; the breeders' association was formed and the herd-book opened in 1970 or 1971, per FAO DAD-IS as cited there.
Wikipedia: dual-purpose, for both milk and meat.

Wikipedia, citing the Bureau des Ressources Génétiques: the 2015 total was estimated at 62,500 to 67,500, with about 25,000 breeding cows. The count given is the midpoint of that range, worked out here, so it is estimated.
Wikipedia, citing Dervillé et al. 2009: about 8,000 kg per lactation of 329 days. The article does not name the recording country.
Wikipedia, citing Dervillé et al. 2009: 4.3% fat and 3.3% protein with the yield above.

facts.v: The breeders' association was formed and a herd-book opened in 1970 or 1971.

sources.text: Wikipedia, citing FAO DAD-IS for the herd-book date.

facts.v: From 1982 breeders introduced Red Holstein blood to increase size and udder quality; the resulting stock was less successful for beef production.

gaps: No conservation status for this breed itself; the FAO's critically endangered rating is for the Armorican, its ancestor. The yield's recording country and year are not given. The 2015 population is a range, so the count is its midpoint, flagged as estimated.
